probes.question: By up to how much can this effect extend apparent durations?
True or false: visual information collected during a saccade is suppressed.

image.alt: An ornate gilded antique wall clock with a round white face and Arabic numerals against a plain pale wall.

body.claim: The second hand of an analog clock can appear to stay still for longer than normal when you first look at it.
body.why: After a quick eye movement (a saccade), the new target can seem to have been seen for longer, and this can extend apparent durations by up to half a second. During a saccade, visual information is suppressed, and the gap in perception is “filled in” with information gathered after the saccade.
